body.statement: Assume \(d_e(G)<\infty\), a valid source-prime chart package \(\mathfrak C_{G,e}\) is supplied, and fix a successful finite output of \(\mathrm{thm:conditional\mbox{-}geometric\mbox{-}resolution}\). Work on the resulting certificate event, on which \(h_{G,e}\) is nonzero. The real supported source set \(\{(\Lambda,\Omega):\Lambda\in\mathbb R^D,\ \Omega\succ0,\ \Omega_{ij}=0\text{ if }i\leftrightarrow j\notin B\}\) is Euclidean open in its support space and Zariski dense in the complex source space. Since \(\mathcal E_{G,e}\) is proper on the model image, there is a real supported source point \((\Lambda_0,\Omega_0)\) whose covariance \(\Sigma_0\) lies in \(\mathcal M_G\setminus\mathcal E_{G,e}\). A smooth semialgebraic stratification refined by the real-lifting sign conditions contains \(\Sigma_0\) in a connected cell \(\mathcal C_{G,e}\) on which real-extension status is constant, and a sufficiently small closed chart ball gives a nonempty compact \(\mathcal K_G\subset\mathcal C_{G,e}\) with nonempty relative interior. For every \(\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G\), \(\mathcal R_e(G,\Sigma)\ne\varnothing\), because membership in \(\mathcal M_G\) supplies at least one complete real supported \(\Lambda\).
body.proof_tex:
Work under the valid-chart and successful-output antecedents.  On this event, \(\mathrm{thm:exceptional\mbox{-}set\mbox{-}validity}\) says that \(h_{G,e}\) is nonzero in the covariance-model coordinate ring.  Identify the free real entries of \((\Lambda,\Omega)\), subject only to the graph support, with \(\mathbb R^N\), where
\[
 N=|D|+|B|+n.
\]
The supported positive-definite source set
\[
 \mathcal S_+=\{(\Lambda,\Omega)\in\mathbb R^N:\Omega\succ0\}
\tag{44}
\]
is nonempty because it contains \((0,I_n)\), and is Euclidean open because strict positive definiteness is stable under small perturbations.  It is Zariski dense in the corresponding complex source space: it contains a real open box about \((0,I_n)\); a complex polynomial vanishing on that box is zero by successively regarding it as a univariate polynomial in each coordinate.

For the fixed acyclic graph, define
\[
 \Phi_G(\Lambda,\Omega)
 =(I_n-\Lambda)^{-\mathsf T}\Omega(I_n-\Lambda)^{-1}.
\tag{45}
\]
In a topological order \(\Lambda^n=0\), so each inverse is the finite polynomial \(I_n+\Lambda+\cdots+\Lambda^{n-1}\); hence \(\Phi_G\) is polynomial.  Nonzeroness of \(h_{G,e}\) in \(R_G\) means that \(h_{G,e}\circ\Phi_G\) is a nonzero source polynomial.  Zariski density of (44) supplies \((\Lambda_0,\Omega_0)\in\mathcal S_+\) with
\[
 h_{G,e}(\Phi_G(\Lambda_0,\Omega_0))\ne0.
\]
Putting \(\Sigma_0=\Phi_G(\Lambda_0,\Omega_0)\) gives
\[
 \Sigma_0\in\mathcal M_G\setminus\mathcal E_{G,e}.
\tag{46}
\]

The model image is semialgebraic: it is the projection of the source set defined by the polynomial covariance identities, the linear missing-support equalities, and the strict principal-minor inequalities for \(\Omega\succ0\); \(\mathrm{lem:effective\mbox{-}real\mbox{-}quantifier\mbox{-}elimination}\) removes the source variables.  The exceptional complement and every real-lifting sign condition are semialgebraic.  Outside the leading-coefficient and squarefreeness factors, the degree of \(p_e(\Sigma,\cdot)\) is fixed and all roots are simple.  The assertion that \(z\) is the \(j\)-th ordered real root is a first-order ordered-field formula, and quantifier elimination makes its graph semialgebraic.  Intersecting that graph with the lifting formula and projecting shows that the locus on which the \(j\)-th root is extendable is semialgebraic.

Apply \(\mathrm{lem:semialgebraic\mbox{-}stratification}\) to the finite common refinement by the model image, the exceptional complement, the possible real-root counts, and all extendability loci, and then take connected components.  The component through \(\Sigma_0\) is a connected smooth semialgebraic cell
\[
 \mathcal C_{G,e}\subseteq
 \mathcal M_G\setminus\mathcal E_{G,e}
\tag{47}
\]
on which the number of simple real roots and every ordered root's extension label are constant.  This is the cell in \(\mathrm{def:regular\mbox{-}cell}\).

Choose a smooth coordinate chart \(u:U\to u(U)\subseteq\mathbb R^s\) about \(\Sigma_0\).  If \(s>0\), choose \(\rho>0\) with \(\overline B(u(\Sigma_0),\rho)\subset u(U)\), and set
\[
 \mathcal K_G=u^{-1}\!\left(\overline B(u(\Sigma_0),\rho)\right).
\tag{48}
\]
If \(s=0\), set \(\mathcal K_G=\{\Sigma_0\}\).  In both cases \(\mathcal K_G\) is nonempty, compact, and has nonempty relative interior in \(\mathcal C_{G,e}\), as required by \(\mathrm{def:regular\mbox{-}class}\).

For any \(\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G\), membership in \(\mathcal M_G\) supplies real supported \(\Lambda\) and \(\Omega\succ0\) satisfying (45).  Rearrangement gives
\[
 \Omega=(I_n-\Lambda)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma(I_n-\Lambda).
\]
At every missing bidirected pair, its entry is \(F_{ij}(\Lambda,\Sigma)=0\).  Hence the real value \(\lambda_e\) has a complete real supported extension and belongs to \(\mathcal R_e(G,\Sigma)\).  Thus \(\mathcal R_e(G,\Sigma)\ne\varnothing\) everywhere on \(\mathcal K_G\).
body.justification: The regular statistical domain must be shown nonvacuous and its real identified set must be nonempty rather than imposed by assumption.
body.gap: Standard stratification arguments isolate smooth cells, but the stated lemma ties such a cell to the certified SEM exceptional locus and to rootwise real extension.
body.consumer: The inference theorem obtains a genuine compact operating region and a nonempty target set on every data-generating covariance in that region.
